label: Fibreglass
summary: Fine glass fibres in loft and duct insulation, boat hulls, baths, panels and circuit boards. They make skin itch and burn and irritate eyes and lungs, and cutting or grinding fibreglass makes clouds of fine dust. Older loose-fill and mineral insulation may also contain asbestos.
signs: Pink, yellow, white or brown fluffy batts and rolls
Duct wrap and boards in heating and cooling systems
Boat hulls, shower trays, kayaks, roof sheets and ladder rails
Circuit board material and fibre-reinforced plastic panels
A glittery, fibrous edge where something has been cut
do: Cover all skin and wear a mask and goggles
Handle batts gently and bag them before moving them
Wet the surface, or cut slowly by hand, to keep dust down
Rinse skin with cool water first, then wash with soap
dont: Don't rub or scratch itchy skin
Don't blow fibres off with compressed air
Don't grind or sand fibreglass indoors
Don't sleep in clothes you worked in
ppe: An N95 or P2 mask or better
firstAid: Skin: rinse with running water and lift fibres off with sticky tape; don't rub
Eyes: rinse with clean water for at least 15 minutes; get medical help if pain continues
Cough and throat irritation usually pass in a day or two; breathlessness that doesn't pass needs medical care
